title: Motility Test
principle: Motile organisms possess flagella and can actively move through a semisolid medium, producing visible growth spreading away from the original stab line. Non-motile organisms grow only along the stab line itself.
purpose: Distinguishes motile from non-motile organisms as one differentiating character in identification workflows (e.g. within the Enterobacteriaceae, or alongside SIM medium's indole and hydrogen sulfide reactions).
reagents: Semisolid motility test medium (e.g. Motility Test Medium or SIM medium)

procedure.instruction: Using a straight inoculating needle (not a loop), stab a pure culture colony once, straight down the center of the semisolid medium in a test tube, to about two-thirds of the medium's depth.
Withdraw the needle along the same stab line used to enter, to avoid unnecessarily disturbing the surrounding medium.
Incubate at the appropriate temperature for the organism, typically for 18-48 hours.
Examine for growth pattern relative to the stab line.

positiveResult: Diffuse, hazy growth spreading outward from the stab line through the medium (and sometimes visible as clouding of the whole tube).
negativeResult: Growth confined sharply to the stab line, with the surrounding medium remaining clear.
interpretation: Motility is a supportive, not standalone, identification character and is typically interpreted alongside other biochemical and morphological results.
precautions: Stab straight down and withdraw along the same path — an off-axis or wavering stab can create a false appearance of spreading growth.
Use a fresh, pure culture; an old or contaminated culture can give an ambiguous result.
limitations: Some organisms are motile only within a specific temperature range (e.g. some Listeria species show motility better at room temperature than at 37°C) — a negative result at one incubation temperature does not always rule out motility.
Overly vigorous stabbing can mechanically distribute cells away from the stab line, mimicking a positive result in a non-motile organism.
